title: Anyone reads reports: the home page shows the newest, /reports/<slug> opens any, each in a script-free sandboxed iframe from an isolated path
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

C2 (derived from 'with the same layout as the reader page' / SC-004 'the home page is that same page and handler'): / and /reports/<slug> render one shared template with the site header (anchor sign-in, sign-out form, owner's Admin link): missing

C4 (derived from the slice's isolation statements): draft, unpublished, deleted and unknown slugs get byte-identical 404s on /reports/{slug} and /raw/{slug}: missing

C5 (from the title and SC-006): the reader pages frame the report in an iframe sandboxed WITHOUT allow-scripts (exactly 'allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox', no allow-same-origin/top-navigation/forms) with src /raw/<slug>: missing

C6 (from the title and SC-006 'from an isolated path, with a CSP that blocks all scripts'): GET /raw/{slug} serves published report bytes only, through serveRaw with the report CSP (sandbox tokens, default-src 'none', script-src 'none', style-src 'unsafe-inline', img-src data:, font-src data:, frame-ancestors <origin>) replacing the site CSP, with nosniff, Content-Type, CORP, ETag, no-cache, HEAD and 304: partial
C7 (from SC-006 'never inlined into the site's pages'): a sentinel in the report bytes appears in neither / nor /reports/<slug>: partial

C8 (from the title 'script-free' and SC-006): in a real browser no report script runs, framed via /reports/<slug> or top-level via /raw/<slug> (design: TestReportScriptsNeverRun, headless Edge): missing

framed-report-links-still-work: needs first: A design decision on how reader-page external links will work. The reader page's CSP has `frame-src 'self'`. It blocks plain target-less links in the framed report whenever they point to another origin, and `frame-ancestors 'none'` blocks plain same-site links too. The options are to widen the reader page's `frame-src` (this stops the block on external links but weakens the policy), to rewrite report anchors to target="_blank" at upload or serve time, or to tell authors to add target="_blank". Note that `<base target>` is not available because `rawCSP` sets base-uri 'none'. None of these options was tested here.
Template name: practice report.html, crossdomain reader.html. report.html chosen, the name the epic design and the build check already use.
Where the public raw handler lives: practice reader.go, crossdomain raw.go beside serveRaw. raw.go chosen, so the whole byte path is one file.

Reader-page caching: practice adds no Cache-Control and defers to Q-007, crossdomain sends 'private, no-cache'. The latter chosen, because it is correct under either answer to Q-007 and answers neither.
An 'Open in its own tab' anchor to /raw/<slug> (crossdomain): dropped, because it advertises a second, bare URL and its value rests on unmeasured top-level link behaviour.
Sign-in return: a Next field (practice) or a SignInNext() method defaulting to '/' (crossdomain). The method chosen.
Sentinel coverage: extend the existing TestReportBytesNeverAppearInSitePages (practice) or add a reader-specific test and leave it untouched (crossdomain). The new test chosen.

Browser test gating: practice gates on HBAND_TEST_BROWSER only, crossdomain also uses the default Edge path. Merged: the default path is used when the variable is unset, and the variable, once set, forbids a skip.

Assay size: crossdomain offered to cut five wells to three. Kept at six, the https well included, because the attribute-alone and CSP-alone wells each prove one of the two layers the constraint names.

The Page.captureScreenshot DevTools fallback behind Shot. Not needed: the CLI --screenshot capture shows out-of-process iframe pixels, measured here (W4 red 805,759, W3 green 805,754, W5 blank 0/0, W1 green 1.1M), and the controls would have failed the run had it not.

No 'open in its own tab' anchor and no rewrite of report links, as the design decided. The blocked target-less link is this project's own frame-src policy, so there is no workaround setting; the upload form carries the one-sentence target=_blank hint.

A person should look at the reader page, the screenshots under HBAND_TEST_ARTIFACTS from TestReportScriptsNeverRun, and a phone-width window (lesson #184). I looked at desktop-width screenshots from the real binary: header, title, date, permalink and the framed report read correctly. Phone width was not looked at.

The reader page cannot be declared as a screen: the app starts only from HBAND_* environment variables (owner ID, GitHub client secret, data dir), which a bare command cannot carry, so `screens` and `app` are left empty rather than declared with a command that would exit 2. The page was opened by the browser assay and by my own Edge run of the built binary.

Q-007 stays open. The reader pages send Cache-Control: private, no-cache, which is correct under either answer but does not say whether the VPS proxy may cache them. Q-006 is untouched: /raw reads no identity, so the cookie question does not arise on this path.

An upload-time notice for target-less outward links in an uploaded report (warn only, never refuse or rewrite) is still a candidate; this slice only states the target=_blank contract in the upload form.
The assay covers Edge 158 only (Firefox and Safari are a known limit). The HTTP tests pin the exact headers and the iframe attribute every browser receives.

The widened rules use internal/** and **/testdata/** globs. I could only check them with the repository's own rules test, because PyYAML is not installed and I have no Fitness tool, so the engine's Fitness op=check should be run once to confirm it parses them and skips testdata the same way.

The design says each shot is copied to HBAND_TEST_ARTIFACTS/<name>.png but gave Shot nothing to name it from, and W1 and W1s could not be told apart by test name.

deviation: The design's three fitness rules (already in the working tree, uncommitted, when the build began) were revised as findings m4 and m5 prescribed. The template rule's glob widened from internal/**/templates/** to internal/**, a separate frame-element rule was added, the OpenRaw check became a token rule of its own, and the byte-path rule widened from internal/**/*.go to **/*.go with http.Dir, http.FileServer and os.DirFS added. The rule files and corpus carry the revised form.

Added TestReagentShape, which is not in the design, to pin the reagent properties m2 depends on.

critique-review missed: The final m4 prescription excepted '**/*.go' from both frame rules ('only the audited templates contain a frame element' and the sandbox-token rule). The stated reason was that the string-literal rule covers Go. It fires only on a literal that starts with markup. So fmt.Fprintf(w, "Report: %s <iframe src=/raw/%s>", ...) at internal/server/reader.go trips no rule, and the corpus rows frametok-q004 and frametag-q003 pin that gap as quiet. A usable check would be to run the project's loadRules/fires over a non-prefix Fprintf spelling for any rule that excepts Go files, before accepting the exception.

critique-review missed: The m5 prescription added http.Dir, http.FileServer and os.DirFS to the byte-path rule but deliberately kept http.FileServerFS quiet for router.go's embedded static files. os.OpenRoot(dataDir) with http.FileServerFS(root.FS()), the Go 1.24+ traversal-safe idiom on this go1.27.4 toolchain, therefore passed. It would serve <data>/reports/*.html under the site CSP, and the rule's bounded_by claimed to cover it. A usable check would be to ask of every ban list: 'what is the toolchain's other way to serve a directory?' Then fire-test each answer at internal/server/reader.go and cmd/hband/main.go.

critique missed: The design said the zero-beacon assertion on server P was made non-vacuous by W4's /beacon/script at server Q. W4 runs with no CSP on another server, and any beacon from P's /raw would be blocked by rawCSP in any case. So P's check tests request blocking, not script execution, and nothing asserted that the reagent's fires when nothing blocks it. A usable question for the critique: for each 'zero X observed' assertion, which control shows X is observable in that same well?

still unknown: Does the VPS reverse proxy pass /raw/<slug> through with exactly one rawCSP, nosniff and CORP same-origin intact? No stage reached the production path (validations#259). The assay runs in-process only.

still unknown: Does headless.Shot's timeout-kill path leave Edge child processes holding the temp profile folder on Windows (headless.go:97-109)? No Shot timed out in any run, and the N-023 fix for it was waived.

still unknown: Will SC-010 or SC-011 need site JavaScript on the reader page (script-src 'self')? The design chose 'no site JavaScript on reader pages', and the assay's red = 0 verdict only means something while the site chrome stays script-free. A like or comment action done with forms avoids the question. One done with fetch does not.

still unknown: Does the reader page read correctly below 492 CSS px and in the light colour scheme? Headless Edge cannot go below 492 px and rendered dark only. SC-031 asks a person to look, but nobody has an automated channel for this.

went wrong: The epic-level design (219) specified an img-beacon proof of 'the frame rendered' that its own img-src data: policy makes impossible. Only the build-check's live Edge probe found it, so the slice started from a contradicted test plan. Neither the design nor the epic design's earlier review had run the browser.

went wrong: The first risk spike halted on a no-go for framed-report links. That measured the project's own deliberate frame-src 'self' and frame-ancestors 'none' policy, and the design had already settled it as a target=_blank author contract. It cost a halt and a 'built anyway' second pass, and nothing in the design changed.

went wrong: Every first-round prescribed fix put to the critic had a hole (m1-m6). Review effort went into the assay wells and the tripwires, not the product code, where no gate found a defect. The builder had to build the critic's version, not the accepted prescription, six times.

went wrong: Fitness tripwire spelling variants went three laps (critique m4/m5, critic-on-fix, code-review IN-m1/IN-m2/M1) after O-020 and O-021 had closed the class. The slice shipped with the Go-file exception on both frame rules and the os.OpenRoot gap on the byte-path rule open, waived to SC-032 and SC-033. Corpus rows frametok-q004 and frametag-q003 now pin the wrong behaviour as quiet.

went wrong: Code-review #1 did not read 4 of the 13 changed files whole: rule_spellings.json (lines 31-186 of 275 unseen), admin_test.go, site.css and admin.html. The unseen-hunks gate sent it back to 3 hunks. The oversized corpus file was only readable through parsed JSON.

went wrong: The design stage wrote the three architecture rules into the working tree, uncommitted, before critique. The build then had to revise them into five rules after the critique, so the version that was reviewed was not the version that shipped.

went wrong: Phone width was never checked. Headless Edge cannot go below 492 CSS px, so validate's 390 px shot was a crop of a 492 px layout. The only check left is the by-hand SC-031. Validation also ran on loopback with synthetic reports only, and graded contact code, not real.
